bridge_cut.name: Bridge Cut
bridge_cut.description: A small graph at arm's length. A bridge is an edge whose removal disconnects the graph, and the word does real work: most edges are not bridges. So the cut axis carries its own control. bridge removes the edge that matters and the nodes recolour into the two components they fall into; chord removes an edge that looks exactly as important and nothing happens at all. You cannot tell which is which by looking, which is the point. graph=theta goes further, two hubs joined by three disjoint paths, where every edge lies on a cycle and there is no bridge to cut; asked for one the artifact cuts nothing and says so. Components are computed by union-find over the surviving edges on every change, and the bridge is found by definition rather than hard-coded, by removing each edge in turn and asking whether the component count rose. The cut edge stays as a short red stub, because an edge that vanishes cannot be seen to have been the one that mattered. Readable in code via component_count() and has_bridge().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction measured in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. Both values leave the graph in one piece, so no node changes colour and the plate reads STILL CONNECTED either way -- the ONLY difference is that one of seven edges is drawn as a 45%-length red stub instead of a full grey rod. Rods are roughly 9% of the subject's projected area; one of seven of them, shortened by half and recoloured grey(0.65) to red(0.85,0.20,0.22), is 0.09 * (1/7) * 1.0 for the vacated half plus a strong hue change on the rest. FRAME = about 1.2%.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN. Below ~1.2% the likely causes in order are (a) the chord chosen by _find_special being hidden behind a node from the canonical standpoint, which is a FIXTURE problem -- move the camera, not the design; (b) the sweep setting cut to a value CUTS does not contain, which fails in silence and leaves the default; (c) the artifact being under ~6% of frame at hand scale, so a real change is diluted past the measure. Read <out>/_rejects.json and open the PNGs before writing anything down.
predicted_degeneracy.measured_2026_10_13: SWEPT TWICE. Final: cut BITES at 20.32% frame / 49.71% focus, graph BITES at 19.14% / 76.96%, no twins, no inert, cut correctly CONDITIONAL on graph. THE FIRST SWEEP FOUND A REAL DEFECT and the prediction below is why it was recognised rather than explained away: cut=chord rendered BYTE-IDENTICAL to cut=none at graph=chain and graph=tree, flagged as a twin pair. The cause was not the axis. A chain and a tree have no chord -- every edge is a bridge -- so there was nothing to remove, and the artifact stayed SILENT about it while already announcing the mirror case (NO BRIDGE TO CUT in a theta graph). An artifact whose answer to an undefined question is to look unchanged cannot be told apart from a broken one. Adding NO CHORD TO CUT and NOTHING TO CUT removed both twins and took cut from 10.24% to 20.32%: making the conditional case speak doubled the axis. I predicted the WRONG structural pair again -- I named none<->bridge at theta, the measured one was chord<->none at chain and tree -- but predicting that there WOULD be a structural pair, and that it would be conditional rather than inert, is what made the twin report readable in a minute instead of being filed as a dead axis.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, because last time I predicted the wrong kind of pair and the sweep had to teach me: markov_blanket_room's real degeneracy was structural (leak does nothing at shell=none) and I had only predicted a small one. The structural pair here is cut none <-> bridge at graph=theta. A theta graph has no bridge, so there is nothing to remove and the two frames differ ONLY in the plate text, NO BRIDGE TO CUT against STILL CONNECTED. Expect that pair near the floor of the measure, well under 1%, and expect it to be CONDITIONAL rather than inert: cut is only defined where a bridge exists, exactly as leak was only defined where a blanket exists. Read the per-pair rows grouped by graph, never the axis mean.
